What's your story.? How and why did you decide to lose weight?

Well @jqueso I am glad you asked.

My wife and I had our first child back in 2018. Just before she arrived, I quit smoking cigarettes (I was a pack+ a day smoker for almost 20 years). That was a huge change. I still vape to get my nicotine, but I'm working on cutting that out, too.

When the baby came out, and we were skin to skin soon after her birth, she tried to nurse off of my man boob. No lie. We have photos of it. That was my first inkling that I needed a change.

By the time she was 6 months old, I realized how terrible of shape I was in. I was struggling to walk up the steps, even without the cigarettes, while holding the baby. I jumped on a scale and saw 255 - a HUGE number, at least to me.

You see, growing up, I was athletic, in good shape, 6 pack of abs, the whole nine yards. Through College, I drank like a fish and ate like there was no tomorrow - and for the most part, at least as far as I was concerned, nothing was changing that much. But, through college I gained probably 20 lbs in 4 years.

Then, getting out of college, working a desk job, got engaged and married, just really let myself go. I had no reason to look good, I was married. I had no reason to watch what I ate, I would be fine.

I developed IBS-D, largely due to my absolute SHIT diet. Doctors left and right told me to change my diet, and see if it helped. I said fuck off, kept eating whatever I wanted. I had a colonoscopy before I was 30 to try and find the cause - but there wasn't a cause. No polyps, no nothing. So, I just stocked up on Peptol and Immodium AD and went about my life.

Back to when I realized I need to lose weight. I saw 255 on the scale and just couldn't imagine it. I looked at myself in the mirror, HONESTLY, and stopped sucking in my gut. Holy shit, I was a fucking blimp. BMI of almost 35. I realized that if I didn't make a change, I would be 300 pounds before I knew it, and that would only help to accelerate me into an early grave.

So, I took the initiative to try losing the weight. Now, I've tried diets before, in so many words. Eat healther shit, workout more, etc etc. But that never really worked long term, so I decided I'd go out and do some deeper research on diets.

Keto, IF, work out til you pass out, whatever it may be, all of these trendy diets didn't explain HOW you lost the weight - they just said 'don't eat for 16 hours and you'll lose weight' or 'don't eat carbs' and you'll lose weight. That is all complete and utter bullshit. I even considered NutriSystem for Men, but thankfully, I stumbled upon my savior just a few days before I ordered anything...

I stumbled upon THIS sub, over at reddit, and if you all have been there, you know that at least 90% of all loseit members there SWEAR by CICO. I had no idea what CICO was, so I started looking into it, started reading through those boards and really getting an idea of what I needed to do.

So, I downloaded MyFitnessPal and started tracking my food and drink intake, with the goal of just understanding HOW MANY calories I was consuming a day, no stated goal of cutting calories out. Then I worked out my TDEE ad BMR and got a baseline in place for my targets and goals. I used the "lose 1 pound a week" metric on MFP, and set myself up as "not very active". I started working out 3-7x per week (Incline bench from Amazon, $80, 2 25-lb dumbbells from amazon, $40).

I followed the guidelines that MFP put in place, and didn't "eat back" my workout calories. Now, I wasn't 100% on my MFP compliance - some days I went over, some days I went over considerably, but I ended up losing about 12 pounds per month while I was in serious "cut mode" focusing solely on losing weight.

So, I made it through, made some changes to my diet and just overall started thinking about food differently. Yes, even now, I still want to eat deep fried everything, tacos, and cookies. I still do eat those things, just not as often, and not as large of portions.

My best advice aside from logging the HELL out of your food, is to set calorie intake goals per meal. You get your TDEE, and then you set your daily target == (TDEE - 500 cals). OK, so my calorie goal when I was 255 lbs was something like 2200 calories, and now, according to MFP, my calorie goal (still to lose 1 lb per week) is something like 1950 cals. So how do I break it down?

Breakfast: 2 coffees with skim milk, and zero cal sweetner. ~190 calories. (Prior to CICO, I was drinking approximately 800 calories in my coffee drinks EVERY morning - whole milk, caramel drizzle, sugar-filled sweetners). I frequently also added a protein shake/smoothie to breakfast after workouts, so that was another ~250 cals. Total for breakfast is around ~450 cals on days that I have a shake.

Lunch: For the first 3 or 4 months, I just ate salads every day for lunch. I will say, when I realized that CICO truly meant CICO, tahts when I was able to broaden my horizons. You see, when you cover your salad in crutons, dressing, and cheese, your 'low cal' lunch quickly jumps to the calorie count of a sandwich. So, I actually started with a new goal - find lunches that are under or around 350 calories. There are plenty of lunches that qualify here, but stick with what works for you. I found some "low carb" soft taco shells from La Tortilla Factory (had to order online, lowest quantity 80 wraps), that only cost me 70 calories. I put 4 oz of chicken in there, 2 tbsp of LIGHT MAYO, half an apple (diced), and some siracha. That is a satisfying, filling, 290 calorie lunch. So, for those keeping track at home, ~450 cals for breakfast, 290 for lunch, ~740 calories through two meals, meaning I had 1250 or so remaining. Also, if you can help it, cut out that smoothie/protein shake. Not for "IF" sake - fuck IF - but for 'banking your calories for later' sake. I love late night snacks. Always have, always will. Can't have them though, if you've eaten all of your calories by dinner time.

Dinner: whatever we were having, and just log the balls out of it and keep portions small. My wife still hasn't jumped on the bandwagon to lose weight yet (unfortunately, and I'm working on that - tips appreciated), so I kind of had to fend for myself in terms of making sure whatever I ate for dinner stayed within my allotted calories.

Snacks: I stocked up on low cal, pre-portioned snacks. Again, I don't give a fuck about macros, so I don't care how many carbs, sugars, fat, etc are in my snacks. I get some granola bars that are 100 calories. Or Fruit ROll ups that are 90 calories. Or some mini ice cream bars that are 110 calories. OR whatever else I want. But the main thing is, when you're stuffing your face full of snacks, make sure you are logging them in your MFP.

LOG everything you drink and eat. Make recipes for things you consume often times.

WEIGH everything so you know how much you're actually eating.

CHUG water when you're "hungry" - most hunger cues are actually not hunger cues - you've just trained your body to react in such a way that when your stomach grumbles, you feed yourself. Most of the time, a glass of ice water will curb that craving.

So, that turned into quite the novella. perhaps I will steal this and re-format it in a more helpful manner and put it here as its own post.
